Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Time: 09:00 PT / 17:00 GMT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Solutions); Aisha Khan, Tom Reynolds, Priya Nair, Evan Li (Meridian)
transcript_body:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. Quick intros?
[00:08] Aisha Khan: Hi I'm Aisha, Head of MLOps at Meridian. We run a bunch of models for grid forecasting and customer support automation.
[00:15] Tom Reynolds: Tom, cloud architect. We manage AWS and Azure accounts, mostly AWS us-east and eu-west for EU workloads.
[00:21] Priya Nair: Priya, security. I'll be validating compliance and KMS stuff.
[00:25] Samir Patel: Hi all, Samir from Redwood, I'm the SE. I focus on private deployments and performance.
[00:31] Jordan Park: Great. Goal for today is to map your networking constraints and see whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private makes sense - sounds like Private/VPC is the focus.
[00:40] Aisha Khan: Right, our preference is private. We can't have model calls traverse the public internet for EU customer data.
[00:46] Tom Reynolds: Exactly, we need data residency for EU workloads, and for some internal models we want everything in our VPC with no internet egress.
[00:52] Samir Patel: Understood. Quick clarifier - when you say "Private" do you mean Redwood Private in your own VPC (private endpoints) vs a Dedicated cluster managed by Redwood but on a shared network?
[01:03] Tom Reynolds: We want customer-managed VPCs, basically Redwood should either peer into our VPC or we use PrivateLink endpoints. Also cross-account peering is okay, but we prefer PrivateLink for tight control.
[01:14] Jordan Park: Cool. A couple of options common with customers: 1) VPC peering or Transit Gateway peering - low-latency but cross-account peering caveats; 2) AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) - gives private endpoints without full routing; 3) On-prem via Direct Connect/VPN to a Redwood VPC. We'll map tradeoffs.
[01:32] Priya Nair: Important for us: KMS integration - keys must be in our account or HSM. Also audit logs (S3 or SIEM), SAML SSO for console access, and SOC2. Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS?
[01:43] Samir Patel: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS; in some cases we integrate with customer HSMs for encryption-at-rest. We have customers using AWS KMS in their account and we wrap keys via cross-account grants. The exact flow depends on whether the compute is in your account or in a Redwood-managed account.
[01:58] Evan Li: When you say "compute in our account" - do you mean we can run inference on GPUs inside our VPC with Redwood's control plane remote?
[02:06] Samir Patel: Exactly. We offer a private control plane plus in-customer compute (on-prem or VPC) in the Private deployment model. There's also a hosted option where you push data via PrivateLink to Redwood-managed infra, but for your requirement of no internet egress we typically do in-VPC compute or dedicated single-tenant instances.
[02:22] Tom Reynolds: Latency-wise what should we expect if we do interface endpoints vs peering/transit gateway for synchronous low-latency workloads?
[02:30] Samir Patel: Interface endpoints (PrivateLink) introduce a small added hops - usually 2 to 5 ms in the same region. VPC peering/Transit Gateway is generally lower-latency but needs route management. For high throughput, we often see slightly better tail latency with peering. But PrivateLink is simpler cross-account.
[02:45] Aisha Khan: We have bursty traffic during certain grid events, so autoscaling and burst to a dedicated pool is important; can Redwood do burst to a dedicated reserved capacity?
[02:55] Jordan Park: Yes, Redwood Dedicated and Private can be configured with burst capacity and autoscaling policies. If you need hard SLAs for those events we can propose a Reserved capacity contract.
[03:05] Priya Nair: On the networking checklist, do you require specific ports open or public IPs for callbacks? We want to lock down everything outbound.
[03:13] Samir Patel: Typically we use HTTPS over 443 for control plane, but data-plane may require internal IP ranges for model serving. For PrivateLink, you keep the traffic inside AWS and we don't need public IPs. If compute is in your account, all traffic stays in your VPC. We'll send a precise network checklist but plan to allow specific CIDRs and internal ALB endpoints.
[03:31] Tom Reynolds: What about cross-region? Our EU data must stay in eu-west-1. Can Redwood run control plane in US but keep compute in eu-west?
[03:40] Samir Patel: You can split control plane and compute but beware of egress and latency. For strict data residency we recommend control plane in the same region and compute pinned to eu-west-1. Redwood Private supports region-pinned deployments; if you want control plane in your account, we can deploy components to eu-west-1.
[03:56] Aisha Khan: Any constraints with Azure? Some teams use AKS for inference.
[04:01] Samir Patel: We support Azure and GCP in Private mode, but feature parity differs slightly. For this engagement we can focus on AWS first and map Azure later.
[04:09] Jordan Park: Quick product callout - Redwood has prefix/KV cache and batching which affects egress and throughput; we might recommend different quantization profiles to reduce GPU memory. Samir will propose model/quantization recommendations.
[04:23] Evan Li: For auditing we need syslogs and token-level cost traces. Is that part of the Private console?
[04:29] Lena Ortiz: Yes, Redwood Console (private) includes per-token cost traces, model route dashboards, and audit logs. We can push logs to your S3 or Splunk via an integrator.
[04:40] Priya Nair: And SSO? SAML? RBAC?
[04:44] Samir Patel: SAML SSO is supported, and RBAC roles map to console and API tokens. For stricter requirements we can integrate with SCIM provisioning.
[04:53] Tom Reynolds: One detail - our VPCs use non-overlapping RFC1918 ranges but we use a Transit Gateway for hub-and-spoke. How does Redwood integrate with Transit Gateway?
[05:02] Samir Patel: We have customers connecting via Transit Gateway (TGW). You can either peer our VPC into your TGW or set up interface endpoints in each spoke. We'll need account IDs and route tables to configure. TGW is recommended if you have many spokes to avoid many peering relationships.
[05:18] Aisha Khan: Security question - do you have SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO certifications?
[05:22] Jordan Park: We do have SOC 2 and some customers asked for ISO, I'll attach the latest reports.
[05:27] Priya Nair: KMS again - we need to ensure that encryption keys never leave our account; is cross-account grant enough?
[05:33] Samir Patel: We usually use cross-account grants with strict key policies; for HSM-level requirements we can integrate customer HSM with our runtime via a trusted boundary, but that'll be scoped in the Private deployment.
[05:44] Tom Reynolds: Any network-level SNAT required for model pulls or layers of egress?
[05:49] Samir Patel: If compute is in your VPC, then you control egress and NAT; Redwood doesn't force outbound. If using Redwood-managed infra with PrivateLink, we can restrict egress as part of the design.
[05:59] Aisha Khan: Okay. Want to talk about benchmarking - can Redwood help us run throughput/latency tests from our infra?
[06:05] Samir Patel: Absolutely. We'll propose a benchmark plan: models (Llama2-like and smaller encoder-decoder), sequence lengths, concurrency patterns, and we'll run head-to-head in eu-west-1 and provide token/sec and p99 latency profiles.
[06:18] Evan Li: Pricing for Private - is it a flat fee or usage + reserved commit?
[06:23] Jordan Park: Typically a base platform fee for Private plus either reserved capacity or usage-based billing for burstable workloads. We'll include a pilot quote.
[06:30] Aisha Khan: Any blockers from our side to get started?
[06:33] Tom Reynolds: I'll need a network checklist and Redwood account IDs. Also we'll validate legal and security docs.
[06:38] Jordan Park: Perfect - we'll send SOC2, network checklist, and propose dates for the deep technical session.
[06:44] Priya Nair: Please include any requirements for PrivateLink DNS entries or certificates - we have strict cert rotation policies.
[06:51] Lena Ortiz: Noted - we'll include cert lifecycle and private cert requirements in the checklist.
[06:55] Jordan Park: Recap of next steps: Redwood to share security pack and checklist; Samir to draft benchmark plan; Tom/Priya to share VPC details and KMS constraints; schedule deep dive 3/11. Anything else?
[07:08] Aisha Khan: That's it from us. Thanks.
[07:10] Jordan Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with attachments.
